# Independent audit of the raw-moment John theorem

Audited file:
[candidate 43892fde2d187dd5](candidate 43892fde2d187dd5),
Sections 1--7. Result: PASS. No mathematical defect found.

The following points were checked independently.

* Fiberwise fixed-mass rearrangement gives a unique indicator support
  source even at boundary mass/base constraints. Averaging two different
  optimal sources would be fractional on a positive-volume fiber set,
  where the rearrangement strictly improves the support objective.
* Distinct constraint pairs therefore give a strict support gap in every
  continuous direction. Compactness of the unit sphere makes that gap
  uniform and yields the stated Minkowski ball inclusion, including
  lower-dimensional endpoint sections.
* The determinant-root interpolation and strict addition of a ball
  justify strict John-radius concavity. Compact graph convergence gives
  upper semicontinuity and attainment without assuming a full-dimensional
  limiting section.
* At maximum balanced mass, every source fills the selected positive
  fiber. Deleting an arbitrary dominated mass-epsilon source from that
  fiber proves the exact Minkowski difference inclusion. The displayed
  homothetic-source family gives a positive inball in its raw moment
  body, excluding the upper mass endpoint from a maximum.
* The harmonic coefficients preserve both total source mass and integer
  base moment for unequal maximizing masses. Strict interpolation then
  excludes every additional integer point, as well as any nonvertex
  maximizing index, from the maximizing-base convex hull.
* The prescribed slope b in an interior joint supporting plane is
  preserved in the actual ambient cap dual. The strictly fractional
  balanced source supplies coercivity in the integer tilt alone, and
  threshold exchange identifies the maximizing indicator source.
* The augmented John contact cone has the correct signs. Its closedness
  follows from the trace-one feature, and the uniform contact-slope
  bound controls support variations near the contact set. Separation
  plus a small isotropic shrink gives a genuine larger ellipsoid if
  the target vector were absent from that cone.
* Returning from normalized raw moment coordinates leaves the mass
  slope b unchanged. Thus sum(lambda b)=0 and sum(lambda Psi)=d are
  exact; the constituent raw moments and their normalized centroids
  have the stated factors of the selected mass.
* Complementation and strict interpolation give the unique real
  constraint maximum at (M/2,M g_z/2). If g_z is integral, the John
  center divided by the selected mass is exactly the true centroid.
  This is an identification, not a depth claim.

The distinction between arbitrary finite sources and actual compatible
fibers is explicit. In the latter case every feasible integer base
has a positive fiber; for an abstract source with a missing integer
base, the interior-mass conclusion is not assumed. No OC conclusion
is used in any audited step.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
